newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia oilmen's leader says strike on hold.
newsitem.headline: Colombia oilmen's leader says strike on hold.

text.p: The head of Colombia's main oil workers' union said Monday a planned strike would be put on hold pending more talks with the government later this week but warned further arrests of members would spark a walkout.

The 5,700-strong USO union is likely to approve a strike motion at a general assembly Monday evening. But leader Hernando Hernandez said no start date would be set as long as there was progress in discussions, which began Sunday evening, with government ministers.

The specter of a crippling stoppage in the key oil sector loomed after the arrest of 12 men -- 10 of them USO members -- last week on charges of dynamiting oil pipelines and of links to the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest leftist rebel force. Another local USO official was seized in the southwest over the weekend.
"We're ready to continue talks with the government. In parallel with that we will press ahead with strike preparations but would cancel those if there's positive results in talks," Hernandez said.
Hernandez described the crisis meeting with the Interior, Mines and Energy, Defense and Labor ministers as "the first step to see if we can avoid a strike movement".
USO social services secretary Gustavo Triana said no date had been set for the next round of talks with ministers but that it would almost certainly be this week.
Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar, however, said the government was unable to intervene in the investigations against detained union members.
Interior Minister Horacio Serpa said he would try to set up talks with Chief Prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso later this week.
A spokesman at the prosecutor's office was unable to confirm the meeting would take place.
Deputy prosecutor Armando Sarmiento said Friday there were more arrest warrants pending against USO members accused of the frequent attacks on the country's oil infrastructure.
But Hernandez warned: "If there are many more arrests it will make the situation much more complex and would force us to take the decision to strike."
In addition to the arrest of its members, the USO will be looking to voice protest at what it claims are government plans for the creeping privatization of state oil company Ecopetrol.
